get.description:
Return the live, same-project direct prerequisites and dependents for
a task. The `{task}` path value accepts an opaque task ID or a
case-insensitive project-local key such as `OPS-42`. Each direction is
capped at 200 relations and ordered deterministically. The response's
strong ETag is the current ETag of the referenced task and can be sent
as `If-Match` when changing its graph.

200.description: Direct live dependency graph for the task

post.description:
Add the referenced task as one direct prerequisite of `{task}`. The
prerequisite accepts an opaque task ID or a case-insensitive
project-local key. The caller must have `tasks:write`, send the exact
current task ETag in `If-Match`, and send a non-empty,
non-whitespace `Idempotency-Key`. The task must be in the caller's
project access ceiling; references outside that ceiling are masked as
not found. A live claim may be changed only by its owner;
a human administrator may explicitly override another actor's claim.
Dependencies are limited to 200 direct prerequisites and 200 direct
dependents, must remain within the same project, and may not create a
cycle. A successful mutation advances only the dependent task version,
emits `task.dependency_added`, returns the updated task (or the
id/version redacted form for a write-only bearer), and sets its strong
ETag. Repeating the same idempotency key with the same request replays
the original response.
Lifecycle ordering is enforced transactionally for claim, start or
finish transitions, ordinary task reopen or completed-to-blocked
transitions, bug triage/resolution/reopen, semantic column changes
(including bulk updates), and dependency insertion into already active,
completed, or actively claimed work. Reopening a completed prerequisite
with an unfinished active or claimed dependent, or deleting a
prerequisite with live dependents, is rejected; rejected requests do
not change task, claim, graph, comment, or event state.

200.description: Updated dependent task and its new strong ETag

delete.description:
Remove one direct prerequisite edge from `{task}`. The prerequisite
path value accepts an opaque task ID or a case-insensitive
project-local key. The caller must have `tasks:write`, send the exact
current task ETag in `If-Match`, and send a non-empty,
non-whitespace `Idempotency-Key`. The task must be in the caller's
project access ceiling; references outside that ceiling are masked as
not found. A live claim may be changed only by its owner;
a human administrator may explicitly override another actor's claim.
A successful mutation advances only the dependent task version, emits
`task.dependency_removed`, returns the updated task (or the id/version
redacted form for a write-only bearer), and sets its strong ETag.
Repeating the same idempotency key with the same request replays the
original response.
Lifecycle ordering guards are applied transactionally across claim,
start or finish transitions, ordinary task reopen or
completed-to-blocked transitions, bug triage/resolution/reopen,
semantic column changes, reopening completed prerequisites, and
prerequisite deletion. A prerequisite with live dependents cannot be
deleted until its edges are removed.

200.description: Updated dependent task and its new strong ETag
